title: Republic of Nagorno-Karabakh (Artsakh) due to cease to exist under President Shahramanyan's decree
body:
On 28 September 2023, nine days after Azerbaijan's offensive began, Samvel Shahramanyan, President of the unrecognised Nagorno-Karabakh Republic, signed a decree ordering the dissolution of the republic's state institutions. The decree, which was to take effect immediately after its publication, said that state institutions and organisations under the republic's departmental subordination were to be dissolved by 1 January 2024, when the Republic of Nagorno-Karabakh (Artsakh) would cease to exist.

The decree cited the difficult military-political situation and the priority of protecting the physical security of residents. It also referred to an agreement, mediated by the command of the Russian peacekeeping contingent, guaranteeing free, voluntary and unimpeded passage through the Lachin corridor, including for disarmed military personnel with their property. Residents, including those outside the republic, were to review the conditions for reintegration presented by Azerbaijan and decide individually whether to stay in or return to Nagorno-Karabakh.

The republic had been recognised by no country. It controlled the former Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast and, after the first war, seven further Azerbaijani districts. After the war of autumn 2020 it continued to exist in the part of Karabakh under Russian peacekeeper control until Azerbaijan's operation of 19 and 20 September 2023.
